businessType: PE-backed residential home-services platform: HVAC, plumbing, and electrical service and replacement. Platform company plus 6 bolt-on acquisitions across 4 metros. 11 branches, 340 employees, 185 service trucks/technicians, ~$68M consolidated revenue TTM. Sponsor acquired the platform in 2022; bolt-ons closed over the last 20 months.
stage: Consolidated revenue $68M TTM, up 52% YoY — but almost all growth is acquired, not organic (organic same-branch revenue +3%). Consolidated EBITDA margin 9.5%, down from 13% at platform acquisition (-350bps). Average revenue per truck $367k/year (down from $430k pre-rollup; industry top-quartile ~$525k). Technician billable utilization 58% (industry benchmark 70-75%). Net leverage 4.6x EBITDA; recap targeted in 12-15 months.
ownerGoal: Restore consolidated EBITDA margin to 13%+ and revenue per truck to $450k+ within 12 months to support a leveraged recapitalization at a 9x+ EBITDA multiple.
ownerConstraints: Net leverage 4.6x EBITDA; the recap and the sponsor's return thesis depend on EBITDA-margin recovery within 12-15 months, not just more acquisitions.

Three of the six acquired branches still run their original, separate dispatch/field-service software (different from the platform's ServiceTitan instance); no unified scheduling or capacity view across branches.
Skilled-technician labor market is tight: average 9-week time-to-fill for a senior HVAC technician; cannot simply hire utilization up.

Membership/maintenance-plan attachment varies wildly by branch (platform branches 41% of customers on plans; two acquired branches under 12%), driving inconsistent recurring demand and winter/summer demand smoothing.
Seasonality: HVAC demand peaks in summer/winter; shoulder seasons show idle technician capacity, magnifying utilization gaps.
Integration team is thin (2 ops integration leads for 6 bolt-ons); branch managers retain significant autonomy per acquisition earn-out agreements running another 6-14 months.
immediateConcern: Consolidated revenue is up 52% but EBITDA margin has fallen 350bps and revenue per truck dropped from $430k to $367k since the rollup began. The sponsor cannot tell whether the margin decline is dilution from buying lower-quality businesses, a pricing problem, or a post-acquisition operational integration failure. With the recap window opening in 12-15 months, the team must identify the highest-leverage fix before committing capital to either more acquisitions, a pricing overhaul, or a costly software migration.
